findings.title: ZIP root-entry skip bypasses type/security refusal and payload inspection
findings.evidence: The branch continues for m.is_dir() and m.filename in ('.', './') before the flag_bits encryption check, external_attr symlink check, or archive.read(). Inspection of the running interpreter's zipfile.ZipInfo.is_dir implementation shows that a filename ending in '/' returns True independently of external_attr and file_size. Thus a './' member carrying symlink mode bits reaches the continue instead of archive_member_refused, and a './' entry with nonzero payload is not recursively screened.
findings.impact: The new metadata exception weakens the existing ZIP link-refusal boundary and does not establish the stated all-payloads-checked condition. This concerns acceptance of nested archive contents in the copied outer file, not extraction of a ZIP link during restore.
findings.proof_level: Confirmed by helper control-flow and local standard-library source inspection. No additional malicious-ZIP probe was executed; the single requested 33-case gate does not cover this case.
findings.actual_exposure: UNVERIFIED: no real archive or private configuration was inspected; no actual symlink-bearing or payload-bearing ZIP root entry is asserted.
findings.minimum_required_change: Apply link/encryption/type refusal before the ZIP root-entry exception and skip only demonstrably safe payload-free directory metadata. Reject payload-bearing root entries rather than ignoring their bytes. Keep the corresponding TAR exception limited to conventional payload-free directory metadata, preserve member limits and continue checking subsequent members. No scanner framework expansion is required.
findings.proof_required: Add focused synthetic regressions for a ZIP './' entry with symlink external_attr and a payload-bearing './' entry, plus a safe ZIP root-directory/public-member control. Retain existing root-directory followed by .env, regular-root-file refusal, TAR root controls and prior scope/restore gates. Confirm refusal is a fixed exclusion reason, not a crash.
